summary.value: The paper targets static KV-cache eviction via output-perturbation analysis and proposes a two-stage, plug-and-play selection scheme. Empirical results on LongBench and Ruler show consistent gains over several eviction baselines. However, key concerns remain. The positioning versus dynamic selection methods is only partially convincing; novelty beyond an intuitively output-aware view feels incremental. Evaluation emphasizes single-turn prompts and adds multi-turn SCBench only in rebuttal with limited scope. Efficiency analysis relies heavily on TTFT; per-step overhead and end-to-end throughput under realistic serving regimes are not synthesized in the main text. Presentation is verbose, and the theory-to-algorithm pipeline could be clearer.

reviewer_concerns.value:
The rebuttal helps by clarifying scope (static eviction vs dynamic selection), adding recent baselines (PyramidKV, DuoAttention), reporting SCBench results, showing chunked-prefill latencies, and committing to clearer naming (CriticalKV) and streamlined exposition. It also argues the infeasibility of exhaustive search and provides α-sensitivity, including at 10% cache.

Still open are issues central to acceptance. The claimed “formal” advance reduces to a theory-guided heuristic that aligns with a straightforward output-aware intuition; the novelty relative to prior output-sensitive or selection-based lines remains thin. The evaluation breadth for multi-turn and ultra-long contexts is limited and presented late. Efficiency reporting is fragmented and omits a concise accounting of overheads per step and throughput across context lengths in the main body. The method’s dependence on a two-stage design and a fixed split (α) would benefit from stronger justification and sensitivity in the main text.

reviewer_scores.value:
R1 (4): Added baselines, SCBench, and efficiency details partially address concerns, but skepticism about scope and metrics persists.
R2 (2): Clarifications and added results improve confidence, yet reservations about formality and suitability remain.
R3 (6): Unchanged. Positive but notes lingering questions on clarity and necessity of the two-stage design.
R4 (8): Unchanged. Their specific requests (α sensitivity) were addressed; broader novelty concerns lie outside their critique. Short review
